title: The Tortoise in the Mud Armor
story: Slumberdredge the Mire Tortoise has slept so long in the swamp that a shell of baked mud has sealed her solid across the only causeway, and she snaps grumpily at anyone who comes near. Mr 6 borrows a resonance chime from the reed-folk: each chime sends 250 shudder-points into the crust, but the spongy mud soaks up 40% of every chime.
question: If the crust needs 700 shudder-points of damage to crack apart, how many chimes must Mr 6 ring?
solution: The mud absorbs 40% of 250, which is 100, so each chime really lands 250 - 100 = 150 shudder-points.
700 / 150 = 4 with 100 shudder-points still left over, so 4 chimes is not quite enough.
praise: Taking off the 40% the mud swallows was smart thinking — the leftover crust just needed one extra chime to finish.
hint: First work out how much damage actually gets through one chime after the mud eats 40% of it. Then see whether the last partial chime still has to be rung.
victory: On the fifth ring the mud crust falls away in warm brown flakes, and Slumberdredge — who was only grumpy because she was stuck — carries Mr 6 across the causeway on her clean, shiny shell.
imagePrompt: A numeral-six knight in a little helmet ringing a glowing brass resonance chime before a giant mud-crusted tortoise blocking a reed causeway, misty golden dusk over the swamp with flakes of cracked mud flying.
